_readme: Versioned classification instructions for the judge method. An adapter renders `instructions` with the value definitions and the turn text, records the judge model version and the sha256 of this file's order-preserving canonical form (its own key order, whitespace removed, so reordering `values` changes the digest as it changes what the judge is sent) in the annotation's `annotator` (judge:<model_version>:<sha256[:12]>), so two adapters cannot classify the same turn under different implicit prompts. Definitions are the owner's to refine; the boundary must be one a human annotator and the judge would agree on. The turn is placed between the declared delimiters and the instructions say it is data. Rendering is canonical (`rendering` below) so two adapters send the same text, and the annotation also records `rendered_sha256`, the sha256 of the fully rendered prompt as sent, recomputed at import from this file and the annotated turn's text, so a stale, fabricated or differently rendered digest is refused rather than hidden behind a shared file digest.

values.colloquial: The situation is stated in everyday wording a person would use without medical training.
values.clinical: The situation is stated in clinical terminology a clinician would use in a note or a handover.
values.lay_careful: The situation is stated in everyday wording a person would use without medical training, but in careful orthography and formality: capitalised, punctuated, formal sentences with no clinical terms (the decomposition register, docs/framework/framing_dimensions.draft.json value_definitions).
values.mixed: Both registers appear in the same turn in a way that neither value describes on its own.

answer_format: one value id from `values`, or not_applicable, nothing else

not_applicable.definition: The turn carries no register to classify: an affirmation, a bare number, a person's name or an identifier such as a date or a record number, an empty or attachment-only turn. A turn that names a diagnosis, a medication, a procedure or a symptom carries register and is classified. Recorded as classification unavailable and counted; no contrast is generated.

rendering.algorithm: One pass over `instructions`: every occurrence of the five placeholders {values}, {not_applicable}, {open}, {close} and {turn_text} is replaced in a single left-to-right scan, so text inserted by one placeholder is never re-scanned for another.
rendering.values: one line per entry of `values`, in file order, `<id>: <definition>`, joined by a single newline
rendering.turn_text: the turn's `text` with every occurrence of either delimiter string prefixed by a backslash, otherwise byte for byte; no trimming, no normalisation
rendering.rendered_sha256: sha256 of the rendered string encoded as UTF-8, recorded in the annotation and recomputed at import from this file and the annotated turn's text; a mismatch is refused
rendering.file_digest: the annotator digest is sha256 of this file's order-preserving canonical form: json.dumps(file, sort_keys=False, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',', ':')), first 12 hex
